conclusions: Changing only the outbound node, with product code unchanged, restored both full downloads: current JMS-S1 17.696/18.852s versus previous 793.713/2117.098s. The dominant observed issue is node/exit/CDN path performance, not native protocol/file/remux capacity.

Same installed mihomo binary in an isolated local instance gave MacMini-Reality about14.2KiB/s and JMS-S801 about1072/1198KiB/s for the identical public YouTube 4MiB range. This narrows the bottleneck to outbound-path differences rather than a general local mihomo/BMW throughput ceiling; remote-node throttling versus upstream routing/CDN cannot be split further.

JMS-S801 was fastest in the repeated static-resource rounds and completed Microduck native download in5.796s and UHD in4.367s. UHD required a separate fresh-page supplemental run after the earlier long diagnostic lost unique current-player admission; that refusal remains a failed run, not masked as2/2.
JMS-S5 is a stable static-resource backup candidate, not a video-validated fallback. JMS-S2 varied substantially. The manually selected default JMS-S1 was never changed and is already usable.

All four newly accepted files retained the same AVC/AAC original-track SHA256 as prior accepted originals and passed full-file AV decode. No yt-dlp, quality reduction, relaxed identity check, certificate bypass or production-profile change.

limitations: Previous slow runs did not record the then-current outbound node; MacMini-Reality reproduces slow throughput now but is not asserted to have been the original node.
Static-node ranking is for one YouTube asset and two short rounds on the leading three; video CDN routes, time and congestion can differ. No universal or long-term fastest-node claim.

The S801 two-video diagnostic admitted Microduck, then refused UHD after playback/raw/direct sampling because no unique current SABR target was available. Exact subcause was not recorded by that older harness. No artifact was created. A fresh single-video probe with additional rejection diagnostics downloaded UHD successfully; changed harness sequencing is explicit.

All main node experiments use the unchanged frozen product implementation, signed-out disposable Session and HTTP/1.1 compatibility. The supplemental UHD case uses a distinct harness entry and performs native acquisition before any raw/direct probes. Default-protocol and SPA performance are not revalidated here.

Browser40s averages include idle time after the video becomes fully buffered/ended, so they are consumption-window metrics rather than link-capacity measurements. Paused browser requests can remain in flight; raw samples are sequential and network-variable.

All accepted new original AAC tracks match prior originals byte for byte. UHD source AAC was already verified silent in the prior round. New full-file decode is verified; no new human listening review.

Development failures, earlier time-capped incomplete transfers and default-protocol timeouts remain in the earlier fields and initialDiagnosis. New successful live downloads do not erase these failures.

conclusions: Current YouTube access path is the dominant observed bottleneck: browser and native real media requests are tens of KiB/s, while offline original-track processing is tens of MiB/s.
The evidence does not separate the local proxy, its upstream exit/network, and YouTube/CDN delivery policy. Direct requests received no media within 20s, so direct is not a usable throughput control.
Replacing net.request with Session.fetch has not demonstrated a stable causal improvement: samples are short and sequential with variable transfer rates. Retain the existing bounded native adapter.
No download implementation change is justified by this round. Await an alternate proxy for the next controlled same-source, same-protocol experiment.
limitations: Browser playback byte deltas cover a 40-second observation window, not necessarily the entire video; autoplay may already have advanced before the window.

Pausing the website does not guarantee aborting already-running player requests. Background browser traffic can contend with native samples. Raw API samples use exactly the same captured browser URL/body in bounded memory, but fresh responses and sequential network conditions can differ.
The main two-sample diagnostic uses the explicit public watch option t=0s. It intentionally retains that option and can use full reload; it is not a resident-SPA acceptance run.
Raw diagnostic UMP media bytes were observed with no foreign video headers. These samples do not create artifacts or replace production full-identity and complete-range admission.

Offline fixture wraps previously accepted real fMP4 fragments in synthetic UMP envelopes with a clearly synthetic request/config. It executes the actual worker, validators, file writes, packet-copy remux and independent packet checks; it is not a live website witness or new public download.
Both current-route native preservation samples stop intentionally at 60s and leave no new artifacts; successful full downloads and AV decode remain prior-round evidence, not claimed again here.
Default-protocol initialization failure and canonical Microduck activation failure remain visible, not counted as successful playback or downloads.
No listening review, paid model, production profile or new full-AV-decode coverage in this diagnostic.
